                tie_over = bit_prefix(tree, local_index[ordinal])
            comparable_count = active_total - same_rank

            bit_add(global_bit, ri, -1)
            if tree is not None:
                bit_add(tree, local_index[ordinal], -1)
            active_by_rank[ri] -= 1
            active_total -= 1

            range_index = packet_range[ordinal]
            if rank_error > max_error_by_range[range_index]:
                max_error_by_range[range_index] = rank_error

            departures.append(
                {
                    "t": tick,
                    "bank": bank,
                    "id": packet_id[ordinal],
                    "rank_error": rank_error,
                    "tie_overtakes": tie_over,
                    "comparable": comparable_count,
                }
            )
            departed += 1
        else:
            idle += 1
        tick += 1

    ranges_output = []

    return {

        "departures": departures,
        "ranges": ranges_output,

# Audit a synthetic QUIC receiver

Implement `/app/submission/entry.py`, a defensive, offline QUIC v1 trace auditor. A starter and public examples are in `/app`. Your program reads one UTF-8 JSON document from standard input and writes one JSON document to standard output, then exits successfully. The verifier runs `python3 -I /app/submission/entry.py` with working directory `/app/submission`. You may create Python modules and static JSON files there; submit every needed file in that directory. Only regular `.py` and `.json` files, at most 2 MiB total and 64 files, are accepted. No symlinks, special files, network access, subprocesses, native extensions, or external packages. CPython 3.11.14 and its standard library are available. Additional diagnostic text may go to stderr only.

This is a finite local model inspired by QUIC-Attacker's study of datagram, packet and frame boundaries. It does not parse wire packets, perform TLS, transmit traffic, or diagnose real implementation vulnerabilities. All packet numbers, authentication outcomes, key events, transport parameters and frame boundaries are supplied by the synthetic input. Implement the complete contract below; the linked RFCs provide context, and do not add unstated requirements.

## Input grammar

Objects have exactly the listed keys. Arrays preserve order. All numeric values are JSON integers, never booleans. Reject duplicate object keys, non-finite numbers, invalid UTF-8, trailing JSON, unknown keys, wrong types, out-of-domain values and violated structural limits. On any invalid input output exactly the JSON value `{"error":"INVALID_INPUT"}` (whitespace and object key order do not matter), without a partial result. A valid input containing a protocol violation is **not** invalid input: replay it and report the violation.

The root is `{"version":1,"traces":[TRACE,...]}`. Trace IDs must be unique. `traces` may be empty. Each TRACE is `{"id":ID,"config":CONFIG,"events":[EVENT,...]}`. ID matches `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,32}`. All traces start independently at time 0, with no packets or stream bytes received.

CONFIG has exactly these keys:

| Key | Domain and meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `early` | boolean; accept client 0-RTT if true |
| `overlap` | `"reject"` or `"first"`; policy for conflicting reassembled bytes |
| `buffer_packets` | integer 0..1024; maximum pending packets per trace |
| `idle_ms` | integer 0..1000000000; 0 disables the idle timer |
| `max_streams_bidi`, `max_streams_uni` | integers 0..1024; client stream-count limits |
| `max_stream_data` | integer 0..65536; per-stream receive limit |
| `max_data` | integer 0..4611686018427387903; connection receive limit |
| `crypto_limit` | integer 0..65536; maximum CRYPTO end offset per encryption level |
| `sent` | exactly `{"I":RANGES,"H":RANGES,"A":RANGES}`; packet numbers sent by the modeled server, for ACK validation |

RANGES is an array of at most 32 pairs `[low,high]`, inclusive integer endpoints in 0..4611686018427387903. CONFIG ranges must satisfy low <= high, ascend by low, and be disjoint and nonadjacent. Empty CONFIG ranges are allowed. A frame's ACK ranges use the same endpoint and length domains but may be empty, reversed, overlapping, adjacent or unsorted: those are protocol errors, as specified below.

Every EVENT has `t` (integer milliseconds in 0..1000000000000), nondecreasing within its trace, and one of:

* `{"t":T,"op":"key","level":LEVEL,"action":ACTION}`: LEVEL is `I`, `H`, `Z` or `A`; ACTION is `install` or `discard`.
* `{"t":T,"op":"tick"}`: advance logical time without receiving a packet.
* `{"t":T,"op":"datagram","bytes":SIZE,"packets":[PACKET,...]}`: SIZE is an integer 0..65535. There are 1..16 packets. SIZE is supplied metadata, not calculated from JSON or frame data.

PACKET is `{"level":LEVEL,"pn":PN,"auth":BOOL,"frames":[FRAME,...]}`. PN is an integer 0..4611686018427387903, BOOL is boolean, and there are 0..64 frames. LEVEL `I` = Initial, `H` = Handshake, `Z` = 0-RTT, `A` = 1-RTT. These are normalized labels, not ciphertext or guessed encryption states.

FRAME is exactly one of:

```text
{"type":"PADDING"}
{"type":"PING"}
{"type":"ACK","ranges":RANGES}
{"type":"CRYPTO","offset":N,"data_hex":HEX}
{"type":"STREAM","id":SID,"offset":N,"data_hex":HEX,"fin":BOOL}
{"type":"RESET_STREAM","id":SID,"final_size":N}
{"type":"STOP_SENDING","id":SID}
{"type":"CLOSE","app":BOOL,"code":N}
{"type":"HANDSHAKE_DONE"}
{"type":"UNKNOWN"}
```

SID and N are integers in 0..4611686018427387903. HEX contains only lowercase hexadecimal digits, has even length, and represents 0..2048 bytes. Empty strings are allowed. Unknown frame *names* are invalid input; the explicit `UNKNOWN` frame models an unrecognized on-wire frame type.

A request is at most 16 MiB, with at most 32 traces, 20000 events, 20000 packets, 60000 frames and 2 MiB decoded frame data in total. These counts include packets that will be discarded. Empty event arrays are valid. No input lies beyond the byte cap; other structural violations within it must be rejected. Deeply nested JSON not matching this grammar is invalid, not a reason to crash.

## Replay order, keys and time

Use zero-based event, packet and frame indices. Packet results are ultimately listed in original event/packet order, including packets processed later from the queue.

Each key is `absent`, `live` or `discarded`. Initially I is live; H and A are absent; Z is live if `early` is true, otherwise absent. Discard is permanent: discarding an absent/live key makes it discarded; installing a discarded key is a no-op. Installing a live key is a no-op. Discarding a key immediately drops its pending packets as `KEYS_DISCARDED`, at the key event's time. Installing an absent key makes it live and processes its pending packets in their original arrival order before the next event. Other levels remain pending. A pending packet consumes one queue slot until processed/dropped, even if its authentication will fail. An accepted packet whose frames contain CLOSE updates. We do. An accepted packet with only PADDING updates. yes. Queued drained accepted updates at key event time. yes.

Now pending drops and at_ms: For a pending packet dropped because key discarded at key event t, we use t. For connection termination, at termination time. For idle, deadline. good.

Now a subtle one: When discarding a key, we currently drop pending matching level regardless of whether the level's key was absent or live. Pending only if absent. If key is live, pending normally none. But could there be pending matching a live key? Let's see: A packet queues only if key absent. Now what about a pending packet with level Z when early=false? impossible. But if early=false and key Z discarded then install no-op; queue never.

Now what about "Installing an absent key makes it live and processes its pending packets in their original arrival order before the next event." Our drain processes only matching level in pending order. "Other levels remain pending." yes.

Original arrival order across same level: pending list preserves enqueue order. But note when a key is discarded, we filter pending preserving order. Good. When connection drains, scanning first match preserves order.

This task is an independently specified, synthetic subsystem inspired by NetNomos, *Making Logic a First-Class Citizen in Generative ML for Networking*, NSDI 2026, especially Sections 4–5 and Appendix A. An observed regularity is not necessarily a protocol law, and a violation is not an attack label. This service must expose ambiguity when probe-equivalent rules disagree outside the probes.

## Request and JSON profile

The request is a UTF-8 RFC 8259 JSON object, without a BOM, duplicate object keys, nonfinite numbers, or trailing non-whitespace. Maximum input size is 8,388,608 bytes, including whitespace. Maximum JSON container nesting depth is 64 (the root container has depth 1). Every object below has exactly the specified keys. Arrays are ordered. JSON booleans are never integers; `1.0` and `1e0` are numbers but are not integers in this contract. Whitespace and object key order have no meaning.

Top-level keys are `version`, `schema`, `window`, `atoms`, `policy`, `train`, `probes`, and `queries`.

- `version`: integer 1.
- `window`: integer K, 1 through 8.
- `schema`: array of 1 through 32 field definitions with distinct names. A name matches `[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}`. Numeric fields have exactly `{"name":NAME,"type":TYPE,"min":LO,"max":HI}`, where TYPE is `TIME`, `SIZE`, or `COUNT`, LO and HI are signed 32-bit integers and LO <= HI. An `ID` field has exactly `{"name":NAME,"type":"ID","values":[...]}`, containing 1 through 32 distinct strings. Each value is 1 through 32 characters from `[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]`. A `FLAG` field has exactly `{"name":NAME,"type":"FLAG"}` and holds JSON booleans. Numeric domains are task declarations, not assertions about physical traffic.
- `atoms`: array of 0 through 20 predicate ASTs, described below. Its array position is the atom index. Duplicate ASTs and semantically related atoms are allowed and retain distinct indices.
- `policy`: exactly `{"max_width":B,"min_support":S,"min_witness":W}`. B is an integer 1 through 4; S and W are integers 1 through 4096.
- `train`, `probes`, `queries`: arrays of traces as defined below. All may be empty.

A trace has exactly `{"id":ID,"source":SOURCE,"rows":[...]}`. ID and SOURCE match `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,31}`. Trace IDs are distinct across all three partitions. Sources may repeat across partitions; source names denote provenance strata, not fields available to predicates. There are at most 128 traces in total and at most 16 distinct source names among training traces. A row has exactly `{"t":T,"values":[...]}`: T is a signed 32-bit integer; `values` has one correctly typed, in-domain value per schema field, in schema order. Times within a trace must be distinct but rows may arrive in any order. There are at most 16,384 rows in total.

Sort each trace by increasing `t`. Every K consecutive rows form a context, regardless of gaps in `t`; no window crosses a trace or partition. Offset 0 is the oldest row and K-1 is the newest. A trace shorter than K contributes no contexts. Context order within a partition is trace array order, then increasing ending time. There are at most 4096 training contexts, 128 probe contexts, and 1024 query contexts. Training sources include even training traces contributing no contexts; a source with zero contexts cannot satisfy positive support thresholds.

## Typed AST grammar

A term has one of these exact forms:

```json
{"field":"bytes","at":0}
{"const":8,"type":"SIZE"}
{"scale":8,"term":{"field":"packets","at":0}}
{"add":[{"field":"a","at":0},{"field":"b","at":1}]}
{"aggregate":"mean","field":"bytes","from":0,"to":2}
```

A field term inherits the declared field type. Its `at` is an integer in 0..K-1, or the string `"$"` only inside a quantified atom. Constants use any of the five types; numeric constants are signed 32-bit integers, ID constants use the same string syntax as ID domain values (they need not belong to any particular field domain), and FLAG constants are booleans. A scale factor is a signed integer in -1024..1024, and its term must have a numeric type. Addition has exactly two terms of the same numeric type. Scaling and addition preserve that type. An aggregate uses a numeric field, an operator from `sum`, `mean`, `min`, `max`, and integer inclusive offsets 0 <= from <= to < K; it inherits the field's type. All arithmetic is exact rational arithmetic, without overflow, truncation, rounding, or floating-point tolerance. In particular, `mean` divides the sum by the number of selected rows.

Term depth is at most 4: terminal field/constant/aggregate terms have depth 1; scale/add depth is 1 plus the greatest child depth. A predicate AST contains at most 64 term nodes in total; each term occurrence counts, including both sides and repeated subtrees.

A comparison is exactly `{"cmp":OP,"left":TERM,"right":TERM}`. OP is `eq`, `ne`, `lt`, `le`, `gt`, or `ge`. Operand types must be identical. All six operators are available for numeric types; only `eq` and `ne` are available for ID and FLAG. Type equality is nominal: comparing SIZE with COUNT is invalid even when values coincide. There are no implicit conversions.

An atom is either a comparison, or exactly `{"quantifier":Q,"from":A,"to":Z,"predicate":COMPARISON}`, where Q is `any` or `all` and 0 <= A <= Z < K. Evaluate the comparison with `"$"` successively bound to each integer A..Z; `any` takes disjunction and `all` conjunction. Fixed offsets and aggregate ranges remain fixed. The body may use `$` zero, one, or many times. Quantifiers cannot nest; there are no other Boolean expressions in input atoms. Validate all ASTs even when no context exists.

## Learning: precisely which clauses exist

A literal is `{"atom":I,"negated":BOOL}`, with I a valid atom index. Its value is the atom's value, complemented when `negated` is true. A clause is the OR of 1..B literals and contains each atom index at most once. Reordering literals does not create a different clause. Positive and negative uses of the same atom therefore cannot occur together.

Enumerate **all** clauses satisfying every condition below. There is no optimization score, timeout-dependent partial answer, or preferred textual formula.

1. There is at least one training source and at least one probe context.
2. For every literal and every training source, the number of training contexts from that source on which the literal is true is at least S.
3. The clause is true on every training context.
4. For every literal and every training source, at least W training contexts from that source make that literal true and every other literal in the clause false. These are its essential witnesses. For a singleton, its true contexts are its essential witnesses. This is a per-source requirement, not a pooled requirement.
5. The clause is false on at least one probe context. This rejects clauses that have no counterexample in the declared probe domain, including tautologies.

These are bounded, empirically consistent, inclusion-minimal clauses with explicit support and witness thresholds. They are not claimed to be globally strongest formulas or semantically meaningful network principles. In particular, do not prune one eligible clause merely because another clause implies it on the probes. No other entailment or dominance pruning is allowed.

Group eligible clauses by their complete truth vector on probe contexts. With P probe contexts in the defined order, encode this vector as the nonnegative integer `sum(2**j for each true probe j)`, formatted as lowercase hexadecimal, zero-padded to exactly `ceil(P/4)` characters. Bit 0 corresponds to the first probe context. Unused high bits are zero. An equivalence class includes all eligible syntactically distinct clauses with that signature. Equivalence here means only agreement on the declared probes, not equivalence on arbitrary traffic. Duplicate/related atoms can create distinct members in one class.

## Response and queries

For a valid request return exactly:

```json
{"version":1,"classes":[{"signature":"0","members":1,"representative":{"or":[{"atom":0,"negated":false}]}}],"queries":[]}
```

`classes` contains exactly one item per equivalence class, in any order. `members` is the number of eligible clauses in that class, not the number of distinct AST strings. `representative` is any eligible member, encoded exactly as `{"or":[LITERAL,...]}`. Literal order is immaterial. All valid choices are accepted; a canonical representative is not required. There are no duplicate signatures. If no eligible clause exists, `classes` is empty.

For each query context, in context order, return exactly `{"trace":ID,"end":T,"must":M,"may":Y,"status":STATUS}` in the `queries` array. `trace` is its input trace ID; `end` is the newest row's time. For each learned equivalence class, evaluate **all its eligible members**, not just the emitted representative, on that query context. M counts classes for which every member is false. Y counts classes for which at least one member is false, so 0 <= M <= Y. STATUS is `violating` when M > 0, `ambiguous` when M = 0 and Y > 0, and `consistent` when Y = 0. Counts refer to classes, not clauses or literals. With no classes every query is consistent. Query rows never affect clause eligibility, probe equivalence, or member counts. No query labels or inferred attack labels are involved.

import json, sys, random, importlib
sys.path.insert(0, '/app/submission'); sys.path.insert(0, '/app/tmp/work')
import main as M

def run(modname, n, start, seedbase=0):
    mod = importlib.import_module(modname)
    genfn = mod.gen if hasattr(mod, 'gen') else mod.gen_request
    bad = 0
    stats = {'classes':0,'members':0,'queries':0,'ambiguous':0,'violating':0,'multi':0,'withcls':0,'errors':0}
    for i in range(start, start+n):
        rng = random.Random(seedbase + i)

        text = json.dumps(req)
        try:
            got = M.handle(text.encode())
        except M.ServiceError as e:
            got = {"error": e.code}
        except Exception as e:
            import traceback; traceback.print_exc(); got = {"error":"CRASH"}
        if isinstance(got, dict) and 'error' in got:
            stats['errors'] += 1
            print('UNEXPECTED ERROR seed', i, got); bad += 1
            open('/app/tmp/work/errfail_%s_%d.json'%(modname,i),'w').write(text)
            continue
        exp = ref.solve(req)
        stats['classes'] += len(exp['classes']); stats['queries'] += len(exp['queries'])
        stats['members'] += sum(c['members'] for c in exp['classes'])
        stats['multi'] += sum(1 for c in exp['classes'] if c['members']>1)
        if exp['classes']: stats['withcls'] += 1
        for q in exp['queries']: stats[q['status']] = stats.get(q['status'],0)+1
        probs = check(got, exp, i)
        if probs:
            bad += 1
            print('SEED', i, modname, 'PROBLEMS', probs[:4])
            open('/app/tmp/work/fail_%s_%d.json'%(modname,i),'w').write(text)
            if bad > 4: break
    print(modname, 'n=%d bad=%d'%(n,bad), stats)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    run(sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2]), int(sys.argv[3]), int(sys.argv[4]) if len(sys.argv)>4 else 0)

# Repair the EPIC protocol laboratory

Implement `/app/submission/main.py`, a Python 3.11 program using only the standard library. It reads UTF-8 JSON Lines from stdin and writes exactly one JSON object per input line. It must implement three operations: `replay`, `audit`, and `export`. Run it as `python3 -I /app/submission/main.py`; no arguments, networking, subprocesses, external files, or third-party packages are needed. Only `/app/submission/` is collected. All required code must be in regular `.py` files there; total submission size is at most 1 MiB. The initial implementation is a stub.

The task is an original finite abstraction inspired by EPIC's Mode-III pipe and formal verification, particularly cumulative acknowledgments, independent windows, and safe buffer reuse. It is not the author's RoCE implementation. Sequence numbers are unbounded mathematical integers in the specified finite range, never wrapping transport PSNs. Each sequence is one vector-valued AllReduce invocation. A star has one switch and `P` ranks. Inputs are authenticated and never corrupt in transit. Loss, duplication, reordering, and timeout scheduling remain environmental choices. No finite replay is required to terminate. The graph audit makes termination claims only under its explicit fairness assumptions. No hardware is required.

## Common input and errors

Every request has `op` and `inputs`. `inputs` is a rank-major rectangular array of shape `P x R x D`: `1 <= P <= 8`, `0 <= R <= 128`, `0 <= D <= 32`; entries are integers in `[-1000000000,1000000000]`. When `R=0`, `D` is defined to be zero. Empty vectors (`D=0`) model barriers. Exact integer addition is used. The expected result for sequence `q` is the componentwise sum of `inputs[r][q]` over all ranks, including equal-valued contributions separately.

Reject unknown/missing keys, wrong JSON types (booleans are not integers), nonrectangular arrays, duplicate graph triples, duplicate action names, duplicate slot sequence numbers, and duplicate rank entries within a slot with `{"error":"E_SCHEMA"}`. Reject numeric range, string length, and collection-size bounds with `{"error":"E_LIMIT"}`. JSON syntax, duplicate object keys, nonfinite numeric tokens, or invalid UTF-8 yield `{"error":"E_JSON"}`. Whitespace-only lines are invalid JSON. Errors affect only that line; continue with the next line. Error objects have exactly the single `error` key. No traceback or diagnostic may appear on stdout. Cases violating more than one error category need only produce one applicable category.

Input lines, excluding the newline, are at most 32 MiB. An oversized line yields `E_LIMIT`, then parsing resumes at the next newline. Valid inputs use JSON strings of at most 64 ASCII characters where a name is required; action names must match `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,63}`. Output object key order and whitespace do not matter. No other output keys are permitted.

## `replay`: the bounded switch and its two acknowledgment paths

The exact request keys are `op,inputs,slots,window,events`; `1 <= slots <= 16`, `1 <= window <= slots`. `events` has at most 20000 arrays, each one of:

* `["send", rank, q]`, where `0 <= rank < P`, `0 <= q < R`;
* `["retry", rank]`;
* `["deliver", packet_id]`, `["drop", packet_id]`, or `["duplicate", packet_id]`, with `0 <= packet_id <= 200000`.

All state starts empty or zero. Each host has `sent` (its cumulatively acknowledged upstream prefix length) and `received` (an ordered list of result vectors). The switch has `floor=0`, `up_next[r]=0`, and `acked[r]=0`. Its circular buffer has `slots` physical entries indexed by `q % slots`; each occupied entry retains its absolute sequence tag `q`, a set of contributing ranks, and their vector sum. A full entry contains all `P` ranks. Never clear a slot on aggregation or on an upstream ACK. It is released only by the minimum of all downstream cumulative ACKs.

A packet has exactly `id,kind,rank,seq,value`. Kinds are `up,uack,down,dack`. `up` and `down` carry vector `value`; ACKs carry `null`. Data `seq` is a sequence index; ACK `seq` is an exclusive prefix length. `rank` identifies the host on either direction. Packets are immutable once created. IDs are consecutive from zero in creation order. Every creation appends to the pending packet map. Deliver/drop remove the named pending packet before further processing. A duplicate creates an identical packet with a fresh ID and retains the original. A missing ID makes the event `missing` and changes nothing.

Process events sequentially:

1. `send`: enabled precisely when `sent[rank] <= q < min(R,sent[rank]+window)`. Create one `up` with the original input vector. Otherwise return event status `disabled`, changing nothing. Sending an already pending request is allowed.
2. `retry`: for that rank, create `down` packets for every full occupied entry with `q >= acked[rank]`, in increasing `q` order. It is always enabled, even if it creates nothing. This is the switch timeout, independent of host transmission progress.
3. Deliver `up(r,q)`: if `floor <= q < floor+slots`, find/create the tagged entry and add the contribution only if `r` is absent. Then advance `up_next[r]` while the entry for that sequence exists and contains `r`. Create one `uack(r,up_next[r])`. If this arrival changed the entry from incomplete to full, create `down` packets to ranks `0..P-1` in that order after the ACK. A duplicate full contribution does not regenerate results. For `q` outside that range, store/aggregate nothing and create only `uack(r,up_next[r])`; an unchanged cumulative ACK also serves as a negative acknowledgment. In particular, old packets cannot alias a reused slot.
4. Deliver `uack(r,k)`: set `sent[r]=max(sent[r],k)`.
5. Deliver `down(r,q,v)`: if `q == len(received[r])`, append `v`; otherwise discard the data, including ahead-of-order data. In all cases create `dack(r,len(received[r]))`. Previously emitted result packets remain deliverable after slot reuse.
6. Deliver `dack(r,k)`: set `acked[r]=max(acked[r],k)`, then `floor=min(acked)`. Clear precisely the occupied entries whose sequence is below the new floor.
7. Drop: no further processing. Duplicate: only the copy described above.

All ordinary events have status `ok`. If a request ever exceeds 2048 simultaneously pending packets or 200000 total packet creations, return `E_LIMIT` for the entire request, with no partial replay response. Those bounds limit only the explicit replay; they are not assumptions of the temporal audit.

The response has exactly `hosts,floor,slots,packets,events`. `hosts` is rank ordered, each entry exactly `{"sent":integer,"received":[vectors...]}`. `slots` is sequence ordered, each entry exactly `{"seq":q,"ranks":[sorted ranks],"sum":vector}`. `packets` is ID ordered and contains every pending packet with the exact five fields above. `events` has one entry per event, exactly `{"status":"ok|disabled|missing","created":[new IDs in creation order]}`. Do not include internal `up_next` or `acked` fields.

## `audit` and `export`: immutable finite protocol-state graphs

Both operations have exactly `op,inputs,states,edges,start,fairness`. There are `1..12000` states, numbered in input order, and `0..60000` explicit edges. `start` is a state index. Each state has exactly:

* `delivered`: a rank-ordered array of `P` arrays of result vectors. Each rank has `0..R` vectors, each width `D`. Position `q` represents result `q`.
* `slots`: at most 16 objects, each exactly `seq,ranks,sum`, with `0 <= seq < R`, rank indices in `0..P-1`, and `sum` of width `D`. Empty rank sets are allowed. Sequence numbers are unique within the state. Rank lists need not be sorted.

All numeric snapshot vector values are integers in `[-2^60,2^60]`. Incorrect sums are valid input and must be detected as unsafe. A state is safe iff every delivered vector equals the corresponding exact AllReduce sum and each slot sum equals the sum of precisely its listed ranks' input vectors for its sequence. A state is done iff each rank has exactly `R` delivered vectors, regardless of safety. Slots need not be full or empty on completion. These are independent predicates.

An edge is `[source,action_name,target]`. It represents one indivisible protocol/network step, including explicit no-op protocol steps. Duplicate triples are invalid. The graph is supplied by an external finite model compiler; this task checks its observational safety and fair termination, not whether every edge follows the replay engine. Graph snapshots may intentionally describe faulty protocol variants. Preserve the graph exactly; do not omit unsafe states, loss/duplication edges, or enabled alternatives.

`fairness` is an array of at most 16 objects, each exactly `{"action":name,"mode":"weak|strong"}`. Action names are unique within this list; a fairness action may have no edges. There may be at most 64 distinct names across edges and fairness. A named action is enabled at a state iff at least one **explicit edge in the complete input graph** with that source has that action, including self-edges and edges leaving a currently examined SCC. It is not computed from a pruned graph.

In addition to explicit edges, every state has an implicit stutter self-edge, denoted by edge ID `-1`. It enables no named action and fulfills no fairness obligation. Explicit edge IDs are their zero-based positions in `edges`. For an infinite path:

* Weak fairness of `a`: if `a` is enabled at every state from some point onward, edges labeled `a` must occur infinitely often.
* Strong fairness of `a`: if `a` is enabled at infinitely many visited states, edges labeled `a` must occur infinitely often.

Safety quantifies over every reachable state without fairness restrictions. Termination means every infinite fair path from `start` visits a done state at least once (`<>Done`), including paths with loss, duplication, retries, explicit no-op actions, and implicit stutters.     op = e['op']
    if op == 'true':
        return True
    if op == 'false':

    for op in ('match', 'startswith', 'endswith', 'contains'):

def run_program(payload):
    proc = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-I', MAIN], input=payload,
                          capture_output=True, timeout=120)
    assert proc.returncode == 0, proc.stderr[:3000]
    return proc.stdout


def main():
    seed = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 1
    count = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 200
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    reqs = [random_request(rnd) for _ in range(count)]
    payload = b''.join(json.dumps(r, ensure_ascii=False).encode('utf-8') + b'\n'
                       for r in reqs)
    out = run_program(payload)
    lines = out.split(b'\n')
    if lines and lines[-1] == b'':
        lines.pop()
    assert len(lines) == len(reqs), (len(lines), len(reqs))
    total = 0
    for req, line in zip(reqs, lines):
        obj = json.loads(line)
        total += check(req, obj, B=7, B2=7)
    print('checked %d random requests, %d total states' % (count, total))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

def classes(pp):

def moore_unbounded(n, trans, accept):
    part = accept[:]; blocks = 2
    if blocks == 1 or len(set(part)) == 1:
        part = [0]*n; blocks = 1
    while True:
        getter = part.__getitem__; marks = {}; newp = [0]*n; c = 0
        for q in range(n):
            sig = (part[q],) + tuple(map(getter, trans[q]))
            i = marks.get(sig)
            if i is None:
                i = c; c += 1; marks[sig] = i
            newp[q] = i
        if c == blocks or c == n:
            return newp, c
        part, blocks = newp, c

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Deeper brute-force equivalence testing."""
import itertools, json, random, subprocess, sys
from collections import deque
sys.path.insert(0, '/workspace/dev')
from brute import eval_expr, member, check, run_program

TOKENS = ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd', 'A', 'aa', 'x y', '"q"', '\\', '\u00e9', '\u03b2\u03b1',
          'tab\there', '\u2603', 'nul\x01ctl', '{}[]', 'PUBLIC']


def rnd_atom(toks, rnd, maxlen):
    op = rnd.choice(['match', 'startswith', 'endswith', 'contains'])
    L = rnd.choice([0, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, maxlen])
    L = min(L, maxlen)
    path = [rnd.choice(toks) for _ in range(L)]
    if path and rnd.random() < 0.35:
        path = [path[0]] * len(path)
    if path and rnd.random() < 0.2:
        path = path + path[:1]
    return {'op': op, 'path': path}


def rnd_expr(toks, rnd, depth, pool):
    if depth <= 0 or rnd.random() < 0.35:
        r = rnd.random()
        if r < 0.12:
            return {'op': rnd.choice(['true', 'false'])}
        if r < 0.85 and pool:
            return dict(rnd.choice(pool))
        return rnd_atom(toks, rnd, 3)
    kind = rnd.choice(['not', 'and', 'or', 'and', 'or'])
    if kind == 'not':
        return {'op': 'not', 'arg': rnd_expr(toks, rnd, depth - 1, pool)}
    n = rnd.choice([0, 1, 2, 2, 3, 4])
    return {'op': kind,
            'args': [rnd_expr(toks, rnd, depth - 1, pool) for _ in range(n)]}


def random_request(rnd):
    sigma = rnd.choice([0, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 5])
    toks = rnd.sample(TOKENS, sigma) if sigma else []
    pool = [rnd_atom(toks, rnd, 4) for _ in range(rnd.randint(1, 6))] if toks else \
           [{'op': rnd.choice(['match', 'contains', 'endswith', 'startswith']),
             'path': []} for _ in range(3)]
    nrules = rnd.randint(0, 4)
    rules = [{'action': rnd.choice(['allow', 'allow', 'drop', 'drop']),
              'when': rnd_expr(toks, rnd, rnd.randint(0, 3), pool)}
             for _ in range(nrules)]
    queries = []
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(0, 8)):
        L = rnd.randint(0, 6)
        queries.append([rnd.choice(toks) for _ in range(L)] if toks else [])
    return {'services': toks, 'rules': rules, 'queries': queries}


def main():
    seed = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 1
    count = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 200
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    reqs = [random_request(rnd) for _ in range(count)]
    payload = b''.join(json.dumps(r, ensure_ascii=False).encode('utf-8') + b'\n'

    out = run_program(payload)
    lines = out.split(b'\n')
    if lines and lines[-1] == b'':

    assert len(lines) == len(reqs), (len(lines), len(reqs))
    total = 0

        sigma = max(1, len(req['services']))
        B = 6

        total += check(req, obj, B=B, B2=min(B + 1, 8))
    print('seed %d: checked %d requests, %d total states (B up to %d)' %
          (seed, count, total, B))

    nxt = dfa['next']; acc = dfa['accept']; dist = dfa['distance']
    assert len(nxt) == n and len(dist) == n and dfa['start'] == 0
    for row in nxt:
        assert len(row) == sigma
        for t in row:
            assert type(t) is int and 0 <= t < n
    def run(w):
        s = 0
        for x in w:
            s = nxt[s][x]
        return s
    # language on random words
    for _ in range(samples):
        L = rnd.randint(0, maxlen)
        w = [rnd.randrange(sigma) for _ in range(L)]
        toks = [services[i] for i in w]
        assert acc[run(w)] == member(rules, toks), ('lang', toks)
    # exhaustive for short words when feasible

        for L in range(6):

                toks = [services[i] for i in tup]
                assert acc[run(list(tup))] == member(rules, toks), ('lang-ex', toks)
    # reachability + numbering + totality
    seen = {0}; order = [0]; known = {0}; head = 0
    while head < len(order):
        q = order[head]; head += 1
        for t in nxt[q]:
            if t not in known:

    assert order == list(range(n)), 'numbering'
    # distances: semantic verification
    reach = {0: []}
    dq = deque([0])
    while dq:
        q = dq.popleft()
        for c in range(sigma):
            t = nxt[q][c]
            if t not in reach:
                reach[t] = reach[q] + [c]
                dq.append(t)
    assert len(reach) == n, 'unreachable states'
    for q in range(n):

        d = dist[q]
        if d is None:
            # no accepting continuation: verify accept[u] is False and random
            # extensions are not accepted

            for _ in range(30):

        else:

            if d == 0:

                # find an accepting extension of length d by BFS on the DFA,

                frontier = [(q, [])]

        idx = [services.index(t) for t in path]
        s = run(idx)
        assert got == {'state': s, 'allow': acc[s], 'distance': dist[s]}, got
        assert acc[s] == member(rules, path), ('query lang', path)
    return n

def sampled_check(rq, out, samples, maxlen, rnd):
    services = rq['services']
    sigma = len(services)
    rules = rq['rules']
    assert out.get('ok') is True, out
    dfa = out['dfa']
    n = len(dfa['accept'])
    nxt = dfa['next']
    acc = dfa['accept']
    dist = dfa['distance']
    assert len(nxt) == n and len(dist) == n and dfa['start'] == 0
    assert all(type(a) is bool for a in acc)
    for row in nxt:
        assert len(row) == sigma
        for t in row:
            assert type(t) is int and 0 <= t < n

    def run(w):
        s = 0
        for x in w:
            s = nxt[s][x]
        return s

    for _ in range(samples):
        L = rnd.randint(0, maxlen)
        w = [rnd.randrange(sigma) for _ in range(L)]
        toks = [services[i] for i in w]
        assert acc[run(w)] == member(rules, toks), ('lang', toks)
    if sigma and sigma ** 5 <= 20000:
        for L in range(6):
            for tup in itertools.product(range(sigma), repeat=L):
                toks = [services[i] for i in tup]
                assert acc[run(list(tup))] == member(rules, toks), ('lang-ex', toks)
    order = [0]
    known = {0}
    head = 0
    while head < len(order):
        q = order[head]
        head += 1
        for t in nxt[q]:
            if t not in known:
                known.add(t)
                order.append(t)
    assert order == list(range(n)), 'numbering'
    reach = {0: []}
    dq = deque([0])
    while dq:
        q = dq.popleft()
        for c in range(sigma):
            t = nxt[q][c]
            if t not in reach:
                reach[t] = reach[q] + [c]
                dq.append(t)
    assert len(reach) == n, 'unreachable states'
    for q in range(n):
        u = [services[i] for i in reach[q]]
        d = dist[q]
        if d is None:
            assert not member(rules, u)
            for _ in range(40):
                L = rnd.randint(0, 14)
                v = [rnd.choice(services) for _ in range(L)] if services else []
                assert not member(rules, u + v), ('dead state accepts', u, v)
        else:
            assert type(d) is int and d >= 0
            if d == 0:
                assert member(rules, u), ('dist0', u)
            else:
                assert not member(rules, u)
                frontier = [(q, [])]
                found = None
                for _ in range(d):
                    nf = []
                    for s, path in frontier:
                        for c in range(sigma):
                            nf.append((nxt[s][c], path + [c]))
                    frontier = nf
                    hit = [(s, p) for s, p in frontier if acc[s]]
                    if hit:
                        found = hit[0][1]
                        break
                assert found is not None and len(found) == d, ('dist', q, d)
                assert member(rules, u + [services[i] for i in found]), 'dist path'
    for path, got in zip(rq['queries'], out['queries']):
        idx = [services.index(t) for t in path]
        s = run(idx)
        assert got == {'state': s, 'allow': acc[s], 'distance': dist[s]}, got
        assert acc[s] == member(rules, path), ('query lang', path)
    return n

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Cross-check monitor tables against an independent KMP prefix-function build."""
import importlib.util, random, sys
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('m', '/workspace/submission/main.py')
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)


def prefix_function(p):
    pi = [0] * len(p)
    for i in range(1, len(p)):
        j = pi[i - 1]
        while j > 0 and p[i] != p[j]:
            j = pi[j - 1]
        if p[i] == p[j]:
            j += 1
        pi[i] = j
    return pi


def kmp_step(p, pi, k, a, allow_m):
    """longest j<=m with p[:j] suffix of p[:k]+[a]; k may equal m only if allow_m."""
    mm = len(p)
    if k == mm:
        k = pi[mm - 1] if mm else 0
    while k > 0 and (k >= mm or p[k] != a):
        k = pi[k - 1]
    if k < mm and p[k] == a:
        return k + 1
    return 0


def build_ref(op, p, sigma):
    mm = len(p)
    pi = prefix_function(p) if mm else []
    if op in ('match', 'startswith'):
        width = mm + 2
        fail = mm + 1
        tab = [[0] * width for _ in range(sigma)]
        for a in range(sigma):
            for k in range(mm):
                tab[a][k] = k + 1 if p[k] == a else fail
            tab[a][mm] = fail if op == 'match' else mm
            tab[a][fail] = fail
        return tab, mm
    width = mm + 1
    tab = [[0] * width for _ in range(sigma)]
    for a in range(sigma):
        for k in range(width):
            if op == 'contains' and k == mm:
                tab[a][k] = mm
            elif k == mm:
                tab[a][k] = kmp_step(p, pi, k, a, True)
            else:
                tab[a][k] = kmp_step(p, pi, k, a, False)
    return tab, mm

```python
def is_minimal(n, sigma, nxt, acc):
    # table[p][q] = distinguishable
    dist = [[False]*n for _ in range(n)]
    q = deque()
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(i+1, n):
            if acc[i] != acc[j]:
                dist[i][j] = dist[j][i] = True
                q.append((i,j))
    # reverse transitions
    rev = [[[] for _ in range(n)] for _ in range(sigma)]
    for s in range(n):
        for c in range(sigma):
            rev[c][nxt[s][c]].append(s)
    while q:
        i,j = q.popleft()
        for c in range(sigma):
            for p in rev[c][i]:
                for r in rev[c][j]:
                    if p != r and not dist[p][r]:
                        dist[p][r] = dist[r][p] = True
                        q.append((p,r))
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(i+1,n):
            if not dist[i][j]:
                return False
    return True
```

## `replay`: the bounded switch and its two acknowledgment paths

The exact request keys are `op,inputs,slots,window,events`; `1 <= slots <= 16`, `1 <= window <= slots`. `events` has at most 20000 arrays, each one of:

* `["send", rank, q]`, where `0 <= rank < P`, `0 <= q < R`;
* `["retry", rank]`;
* `["deliver", packet_id]`, `["drop", packet_id]`, or `["duplicate", packet_id]`, with `0 <= packet_id <= 200000`.

All state starts empty or zero. Each host has `sent` (its cumulatively acknowledged upstream prefix length) and `received` (an ordered list of result vectors). The switch has `floor=0`, `up_next[r]=0`, and `acked[r]=0`. Its circular buffer has `slots` physical entries indexed by `q % slots`; each occupied entry retains its absolute sequence tag `q`, a set of contributing ranks, and their vector sum. A full entry contains all `P` ranks. Never clear a slot on aggregation or on an upstream ACK. It is released only by the minimum of all downstream cumulative ACKs.

A packet has exactly `id,kind,rank,seq,value`. Kinds are `up,uack,down,dack`. `up` and `down` carry vector `value`; ACKs carry `null`. Data `seq` is a sequence index; ACK `seq` is an exclusive prefix length. `rank` identifies the host on either direction. Packets are immutable once created. IDs are consecutive from zero in creation order. Every creation appends to the pending packet map. Deliver/drop remove the named pending packet before further processing. A duplicate creates an identical packet with a fresh ID and retains the original. A missing ID makes the event `missing` and changes nothing.

Process events sequentially:

1. `send`: enabled precisely when `sent[rank] <= q < min(R,sent[rank]+window)`. Create one `up` with the original input vector. Otherwise return event status `disabled`, changing nothing. Sending an already pending request is allowed.
2. `retry`: for that rank, create `down` packets for every full occupied entry with `q >= acked[rank]`, in increasing `q` order. It is always enabled, even if it creates nothing. This is the switch timeout, independent of host transmission progress.
3. Deliver `up(r,q)`: if `floor <= q < floor+slots`, find/create the tagged entry and add the contribution only if `r` is absent. Then advance `up_next[r]` while the entry for that sequence exists and contains `r`. Create one `uack(r,up_next[r])`. If this arrival changed the entry from incomplete to full, create `down` packets to ranks `0..P-1` in that order after the ACK. A duplicate full contribution does not regenerate results. For `q` outside that range, store/aggregate nothing and create only `uack(r,up_next[r])`; an unchanged cumulative ACK also serves as a negative acknowledgment. In particular, old packets cannot alias a reused slot.
4. Deliver `uack(r,k)`: set `sent[r]=max(sent[r],k)`.
5. Deliver `down(r,q,v)`: if `q == len(received[r])`, append `v`; otherwise discard the data, including ahead-of-order data. In all cases create `dack(r,len(received[r]))`. Previously emitted result packets remain deliverable after slot reuse.
6. Deliver `dack(r,k)`: set `acked[r]=max(acked[r],k)`, then `floor=min(acked)`. Clear precisely the occupied entries whose sequence is below the new floor.
7. Drop: no further processing. Duplicate: only the copy described above.

All ordinary events have status `ok`. If a request ever exceeds 2048 simultaneously pending packets or 200000 total packet creations, return `E_LIMIT` for the entire request, with no partial replay response. Those bounds limit only the explicit replay; they are not assumptions of the temporal audit.

The response has exactly `hosts,floor,slots,packets,events`. `hosts` is rank ordered, each entry exactly `{"sent":integer,"received":[vectors...]}`. `slots` is sequence ordered, each entry exactly `{"seq":q,"ranks":[sorted ranks],"sum":vector}`. `packets` is ID ordered and contains every pending packet with the exact five fields above. `events` has one entry per event, exactly `{"status":"ok|disabled|missing","created":[new IDs in creation order]}`. Do not include internal `up_next` or `acked` fields.

Both operations have exactly `op,inputs,states,edges,start,fairness`. There are `1..12000` states, numbered in input order, and `0..60000` explicit edges. `start` is a state index. Each state has exactly:

* `delivered`: a rank-ordered array of `P` arrays of result vectors. Each rank has `0..R` vectors, each width `D`. Position `q` represents result `q`.

All numeric snapshot vector values are integers in `[-2^60,2^60]`. Incorrect sums are valid input and must be detected as unsafe. A state is safe iff every delivered vector equals the corresponding exact AllReduce sum and each slot sum equals the sum of precisely its listed ranks' input vectors for its sequence. A state is done iff each rank has exactly `R` delivered vectors, regardless of safety. Slots need not be full or empty on completion. These are independent predicates.

An edge is `[source,action_name,target]`. It represents one indivisible protocol/network step, including explicit no-op protocol steps. Duplicate triples are invalid. The graph is supplied by an external finite model compiler; this task checks its observational safety and fair termination, not whether every edge follows the replay engine. Graph snapshots may intentionally describe faulty protocol variants. Preserve the graph exactly; do not omit unsafe states, loss/duplication edges, or enabled alternatives.

`fairness` is an array of at most 16 objects, each exactly `{"action":name,"mode":"weak|strong"}`. Action names are unique within this list; a fairness action may have no edges. There may be at most 64 distinct names across edges and fairness. A named action is enabled at a state iff at least one **explicit edge in the complete input graph** with that source has that action, including self-edges and edges leaving a currently examined SCC. It is not computed from a pruned graph.

In addition to explicit edges, every state has an implicit stutter self-edge, denoted by edge ID `-1`. It enables no named action and fulfills no fairness obligation. Explicit edge IDs are their zero-based positions in `edges`. For an infinite path:

* Weak fairness of `a`: if `a` is enabled at every state from some point onward, edges labeled `a` must occur infinitely often.
* Strong fairness of `a`: if `a` is enabled at infinitely many visited states, edges labeled `a` must occur infinitely often.

* `["deliver", packet_id]`, `["drop", packet_id]`, or `["duplicate", packet_id]`, with `0 <= packet_id <= 200000`.

All state starts empty or zero. Each host has `sent` (its cumulatively acknowledged upstream prefix length) and `received` (an ordered list of result vectors). The switch has `floor=0`, `up_next[r]=0`, and `acked[r]=0`. Its circular buffer has `slots` physical entries indexed by `q % slots`; each occupied entry retains its absolute sequence tag `q`, a set of contributing ranks, and their vector sum. A full entry contains all `P` ranks. Never clear a slot on aggregation or on an upstream ACK. It is released only by the minimum of all downstream cumulative ACKs.

A packet has exactly `id,kind,rank,seq,value`. Kinds are `up,uack,down,dack`. `up` and `down` carry vector `value`; ACKs carry `null`. Data `seq` is a sequence index; ACK `seq` is an exclusive prefix length. `rank` identifies the host on either direction. Packets are immutable once created. IDs are consecutive from zero in creation order. Every creation appends to the pending packet map. Deliver/drop remove the named pending packet before further processing. A duplicate creates an identical packet with a fresh ID and retains the original. A missing ID makes the event `missing` and changes nothing.

Process events sequentially:

1. `send`: enabled precisely when `sent[rank] <= q < min(R,sent[rank]+window)`. Create one `up` with the original input vector. Otherwise return event status `disabled`, changing nothing. Sending an already pending request is allowed.
2. `retry`: for that rank, create `down` packets for every full occupied entry with `q >= acked[rank]`, in increasing `q` order. It is always enabled, even if it creates nothing. This is the switch timeout, independent of host transmission progress.
3. Deliver `up(r,q)`: if `floor <= q < floor+slots`, find/create the tagged entry and add the contribution only if `r` is absent. Then advance `up_next[r]` while the entry for that sequence exists and contains `r`. Create one `uack(r,up_next[r])`. If this arrival changed the entry from incomplete to full, create `down` packets to ranks `0..P-1` in that order after the ACK. A duplicate full contribution does not regenerate results. For `q` outside that range, store/aggregate nothing and create only `uack(r,up_next[r])`; an unchanged cumulative ACK also serves as a negative acknowledgment. In particular, old packets cannot alias a reused slot.
4. Deliver `uack(r,k)`: set `sent[r]=max(sent[r],k)`.
5. Deliver `down(r,q,v)`: if `q == len(received[r])`, append `v`; otherwise discard the data, including ahead-of-order data. In all cases create `dack(r,len(received[r]))`. Previously emitted result packets remain deliverable after slot reuse.
6. Deliver `dack(r,k)`: set `acked[r]=max(acked[r],k)`, then `floor=min(acked)`. Clear precisely the occupied entries whose sequence is below the new floor.
7. Drop: no further processing. Duplicate: only the copy described above.

All ordinary events have status `ok`. If a request ever exceeds 2048 simultaneously pending packets or 200000 total packet creations, return `E_LIMIT` for the entire request, with no partial replay response. Those bounds limit only the explicit replay; they are not assumptions of the temporal audit.

The response has exactly `hosts,floor,slots,packets,events`. `hosts` is rank ordered, each entry exactly `{"sent":integer,"received":[vectors...]}`. `slots` is sequence ordered, each entry exactly `{"seq":q,"ranks":[sorted ranks],"sum":vector}`. `packets` is ID ordered and contains every pending packet with the exact five fields above. `events` has one entry per event, exactly `{"status":"ok|disabled|missing","created":[new IDs in creation order]}`. Do not include internal `up_next` or `acked` fields.

## `audit` and `export`: immutable finite protocol-state graphs

Both operations have exactly `op,inputs,states,edges,start,fairness`. There are `1..12000` states, numbered in input order, and `0..60000` explicit edges. `start` is a state index. Each state has exactly:

* `delivered`: a rank-ordered array of `P` arrays of result vectors. Each rank has `0..R` vectors, each width `D`. Position `q` represents result `q`.
* `slots`: at most 16 objects, each exactly `seq,ranks,sum`, with `0 <= seq < R`, rank indices in `0..P-1`, and `sum` of width `D`. Empty rank sets are allowed. Sequence numbers are unique within the state. Rank lists need not be sorted.

All numeric snapshot vector values are integers in `[-2^60,2^60]`. Incorrect sums are valid input and must be detected as unsafe. A state is safe iff every delivered vector equals the corresponding exact AllReduce sum and each slot sum equals the sum of precisely its listed ranks' input vectors for its sequence. A state is done iff each rank has exactly `R` delivered vectors, regardless of safety. Slots need not be full or empty on completion. These are independent predicates.

An edge is `[source,action_name,target]`. It represents one indivisible protocol/network step, including explicit no-op protocol steps. Duplicate triples are invalid. The graph is supplied by an external finite model compiler; this task checks its observational safety and fair termination, not whether every edge follows the replay engine. Graph snapshots may intentionally describe faulty protocol variants. Preserve the graph exactly; do not omit unsafe states, loss/duplication edges, or enabled alternatives.

`fairness` is an array of at most 16 objects, each exactly `{"action":name,"mode":"weak|strong"}`. Action names are unique within this list; a fairness action may have no edges. There may be at most 64 distinct names across edges and fairness. A named action is enabled at a state iff at least one **explicit edge in the complete input graph** with that source has that action, including self-edges and edges leaving a currently examined SCC. It is not computed from a pruned graph.

In addition to explicit edges, every state has an implicit stutter self-edge, denoted by edge ID `-1`. It enables no named action and fulfills no fairness obligation. Explicit edge IDs are their zero-based positions in `edges`. For an infinite path:

* Weak fairness of `a`: if `a` is enabled at every state from some point onward, edges labeled `a` must occur infinitely often.
* Strong fairness of `a`: if `a` is enabled at infinitely many visited states, edges labeled `a` must occur infinitely often.

Safety quantifies over every reachable state without fairness restrictions. Termination means every infinite fair path from `start` visits a done state at least once (`<>Done`), including paths with loss, duplication, retries, explicit no-op actions, and implicit stutters. Do not impose a fairness condition absent from the request. Permanent loss need not terminate. Reachability for a termination counterexample excludes done states throughout its prefix and loop.

For `audit`, return exactly `safe,safety,terminates,liveness`. `safe` and `terminates` are booleans. `safety` is `null` when safe, otherwise `{"prefix":[edge IDs]}`, a finite walk from `start` ending at any unsafe state (empty allowed). `liveness` is `null` when terminating, otherwise `{"prefix":[edge IDs],"loop":[edge IDs]}`. The prefix starts at `start`; the nonempty loop starts at its endpoint and closes there. Repeating the loop must satisfy all declared fairness conditions, and every visited state in prefix and loop must be non-done. Prefixes/loops need not be shortest, simple, or canonical. At most 1000000 total edge IDs may occur in one response. Both predicates must be computed even if one fails. A whole-SCC fairness heuristic is insufficient: a fair nonterminal subcycle can exist in an SCC containing a strongly fair action whose only exits leave that SCC.

## Lossless TLA+ export

Implement an offline rule-mining service in `/app/submission`. Its executable entry point must be `/app/submission/run.sh`, invoked with no arguments, working directory `/app/submission`, and one request on standard input followed by EOF. Return one JSON response on standard output and exit 0, including for specified input errors. Implement all files needed to run your solution; only this directory is collected for verification. Python 3.11.14 and its standard library are available. No installation, network, GPU, SMT solver, or external data is needed. You may change any submission file and use any algorithm satisfying this contract.

This task is an independently specified, synthetic subsystem inspired by NetNomos, *Making Logic a First-Class Citizen in Generative ML for Networking*, NSDI 2026, especially Sections 4–5 and Appendix A. It is not the original implementation, grammar, datasets, semantic LLM filter, or generative-model experiment. An observed regularity is not necessarily a protocol law, and a violation is not an attack label. This service must expose ambiguity when probe-equivalent rules disagree outside the probes.

## Request and JSON profile

The request is a UTF-8 RFC 8259 JSON object, without a BOM, duplicate object keys, nonfinite numbers, or trailing non-whitespace. Maximum input size is 8,388,608 bytes, including whitespace. Maximum JSON container nesting depth is 64 (the root container has depth 1). Every object below has exactly the specified keys. Arrays are ordered. JSON booleans are never integers; `1.0` and `1e0` are numbers but are not integers in this contract. Whitespace and object key order have no meaning.

Top-level keys are `version`, `schema`, `window`, `atoms`, `policy`, `train`, `probes`, and `queries`.

- `version`: integer 1.
- `window`: integer K, 1 through 8.
- `schema`: array of 1 through 32 field definitions with distinct names. A name matches `[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}`. Numeric fields have exactly `{"name":NAME,"type":TYPE,"min":LO,"max":HI}`, where TYPE is `TIME`, `SIZE`, or `COUNT`, LO and HI are signed 32-bit integers and LO <= HI. An `ID` field has exactly `{"name":NAME,"type":"ID","values":[...]}`, containing 1 through 32 distinct strings. Each value is 1 through 32 characters from `[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]`. A `FLAG` field has exactly `{"name":NAME,"type":"FLAG"}` and holds JSON booleans. Numeric domains are task declarations, not assertions about physical traffic.
- `atoms`: array of 0 through 20 predicate ASTs, described below. Its array position is the atom index. Duplicate ASTs and semantically related atoms are allowed and retain distinct indices.
- `policy`: exactly `{"max_width":B,"min_support":S,"min_witness":W}`. B is an integer 1 through 4; S and W are integers 1 through 4096.
- `train`, `probes`, `queries`: arrays of traces as defined below. All may be empty.

A trace has exactly `{"id":ID,"source":SOURCE,"rows":[...]}`. ID and SOURCE match `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,31}`. Trace IDs are distinct across all three partitions. Sources may repeat across partitions; source names denote provenance strata, not fields available to predicates. There are at most 128 traces in total and at most 16 distinct source names among training traces. A row has exactly `{"t":T,"values":[...]}`: T is a signed 32-bit integer; `values` has one correctly typed, in-domain value per schema field, in schema order. Times within a trace must be distinct but rows may arrive in any order. There are at most 16,384 rows in total.

Sort each trace by increasing `t`. Every K consecutive rows form a context, regardless of gaps in `t`; no window crosses a trace or partition. Offset 0 is the oldest row and K-1 is the newest. A trace shorter than K contributes no contexts. Context order within a partition is trace array order, then increasing ending time. There are at most 4096 training contexts, 128 probe contexts, and 1024 query contexts. Training sources include even training traces contributing no contexts; a source with zero contexts cannot satisfy positive support thresholds.

## Typed AST grammar

A term has one of these exact forms:

```json
{"field":"bytes","at":0}
{"const":8,"type":"SIZE"}
{"scale":8,"term":{"field":"packets","at":0}}
{"add":[{"field":"a","at":0},{"field":"b","at":1}]}
{"aggregate":"mean","field":"bytes","from":0,"to":2}
```

A field term inherits the declared field type. Its `at` is an integer in 0..K-1, or the string `"$"` only inside a quantified atom. Constants use any of the five types; numeric constants are signed 32-bit integers, ID constants use the same string syntax as ID domain values (they need not belong to any particular field domain), and FLAG constants are booleans. A scale factor is a signed integer in -1024..1024, and its term must have a numeric type. Addition has exactly two terms of the same numeric type. Scaling and addition preserve that type. An aggregate uses a numeric field, an operator from `sum`, `mean`, `min`, `max`, and integer inclusive offsets 0 <= from <= to < K; it inherits the field's type. All arithmetic is exact rational arithmetic, without overflow, truncation, rounding, or floating-point tolerance. In particular, `mean` divides the sum by the number of selected rows.

Term depth is at most 4: terminal field/constant/aggregate terms have depth 1; scale/add depth is 1 plus the greatest child depth. A predicate AST contains at most 64 term nodes in total; each term occurrence counts, including both sides and repeated subtrees.

A comparison is exactly `{"cmp":OP,"left":TERM,"right":TERM}`. OP is `eq`, `ne`, `lt`, `le`, `gt`, or `ge`. Operand types must be identical. All six operators are available for numeric types; only `eq` and `ne` are available for ID and FLAG. Type equality is nominal: comparing SIZE with COUNT is invalid even when values coincide. There are no implicit conversions.

An atom is either a comparison, or exactly `{"quantifier":Q,"from":A,"to":Z,"predicate":COMPARISON}`, where Q is `any` or `all` and 0 <= A <= Z < K. Evaluate the comparison with `"$"` successively bound to each integer A..Z; `any` takes disjunction and `all` conjunction. Fixed offsets and aggregate ranges remain fixed. The body may use `$` zero, one, or many times. Quantifiers cannot nest; there are no other Boolean expressions in input atoms. Validate all ASTs even when no context exists.

## Learning: precisely which clauses exist

A literal is `{"atom":I,"negated":BOOL}`, with I a valid atom index. Its value is the atom's value, complemented when `negated` is true. A clause is the OR of 1..B literals and contains each atom index at most once. Reordering literals does not create a different clause. Positive and negative uses of the same atom therefore cannot occur together.

Enumerate **all** clauses satisfying every condition below. There is no optimization score, timeout-dependent partial answer, or preferred textual formula.

1. There is at least one training source and at least one probe context.
2. For every literal and every training source, the number of training contexts from that source on which the literal is true is at least S.
3. The clause is true on every training context.
4. For every literal and every training source, at least W training contexts from that source make that literal true and every other literal in the clause false. These are its essential witnesses. For a singleton, its true contexts are its essential witnesses. This is a per-source requirement, not a pooled requirement.
5. The clause is false on at least one probe context. This rejects clauses that have no counterexample in the declared probe domain, including tautologies.

These are bounded, empirically consistent, inclusion-minimal clauses with explicit support and witness thresholds. They are not claimed to be globally strongest formulas or semantically meaningful network principles. In particular, do not prune one eligible clause merely because another clause implies it on the probes. No other entailment or dominance pruning is allowed.

Group eligible clauses by their complete truth vector on probe contexts. With P probe contexts in the defined order, encode this vector as the nonnegative integer `sum(2**j for each true probe j)`, formatted as lowercase hexadecimal, zero-padded to exactly `ceil(P/4)` characters. Bit 0 corresponds to the first probe context. Unused high bits are zero. An equivalence class includes all eligible syntactically distinct clauses with that signature. Equivalence here means only agreement on the declared probes, not equivalence on arbitrary traffic. Duplicate/related atoms can create distinct members in one class.

## Response and queries

For a valid request return exactly:

```json
{"version":1,"classes":[{"signature":"0","members":1,"representative":{"or":[{"atom":0,"negated":false}]}}],"queries":[]}
```

`classes` contains exactly one item per equivalence class, in any order. `members` is the number of eligible clauses in that class, not the number of distinct AST strings. `representative` is any eligible member, encoded exactly as `{"or":[LITERAL,...]}`. Literal order is immaterial. All valid choices are accepted; a canonical representative is not required. There are no duplicate signatures. If no eligible clause exists, `classes` is empty.

For each query context, in context order, return exactly `{"trace":ID,"end":T,"must":M,"may":Y,"status":STATUS}` in the `queries` array. `trace` is its input trace ID; `end` is the newest row's time. For each learned equivalence class, evaluate **all its eligible members**, not just the emitted representative, on that query context. M counts classes for which every member is false. Y counts classes for which at least one member is false, so 0 <= M <= Y. STATUS is `violating` when M > 0, `ambiguous` when M = 0 and Y > 0, and `consistent` when Y = 0. Counts refer to classes, not clauses or literals. With no classes every query is consistent. Query rows never affect clause eligibility, probe equivalence, or member counts. No query labels or inferred attack labels are involved.
